t.title: Audio Agent: a voice assistant for Android
t.description: Audio Agent is an experimental voice assistant for Android for blind, low-vision and motor-impaired users: long voice conversations, documents in chats, music control, timers, reminders and more. Alpha version.
t.alphaText: Audio Agent is in alpha, earlier than beta. It is experimental software made by one person. Expect bugs, missing features and changes without notice. Do not rely on it for anything important or safety-critical, and do not use it as your only way to call for help or to keep reminders.
t.alphaText2: There is no guarantee of support or updates.
t.whatText: Audio Agent is a voice assistant for Android, made first of all for blind and low-vision people and for people with limited use of their hands or other disabilities. You press a button, speak, and the assistant answers aloud. It is not a tool for single commands. It holds a long conversation: the chat goes on for many turns and keeps what was said earlier. You can attach a document to a chat and discuss it by voice. It also plays and controls your music, and does everyday things: timers, reminders, notes, weather, calendar, calls and routes.
t.canIntro: Everything here works by voice. The user guide has the exact phrases.
can: One button is enough. You can talk to the assistant with a single button on a remote (a fob), a switch, or a key: start a recording, stop, replay the answer. If the remote has more buttons, you can give each one a function. On any one button you can set up to six different actions: a short press and a long press, each as a single, a double or a triple press. You set this up on the screen, button by button, and the app can learn which button you pressed.
Long conversations. A chat continues over many turns and keeps its context, so you can ask a follow-up question without repeating yourself.

Documents. Attach a text document (plain text or Markdown) from the clipboard, or with Share from another app. Then ask about it by voice, for example which section covers a topic. A long document is read section by section.
Music. Play by artist, album or track. Pause, resume, next, previous, rewind and forward, louder and quieter. Save and play playlists. Ask what you listened to.

Chats. Start a new chat, go back to the previous one, hear the topics of recent chats, find a chat by its topic and open it, and split a chat in two. On the screen you can also delete a chat, copy its brief summary, and start a new chat from any message.
Timers and reminders, by time or by place. A reminder by place needs location permission.
Notes and lists, such as a shopping list: add, read, cross out, clear.
Weather, the time, news and web search. Search and news need a DeepSeek key.
Calendar: read your events and add a new one.
Calling a contact (the phone dialer opens, you press call) and routes in the maps app, with saved places such as home or work.
Reading your unread text messages aloud, with numbers and codes hidden.
Skip the answer that is being spoken, or rephrase your last question.
A light or dark theme, and a black screen for driving.
t.whatText2: It has no server of its own and no account. It talks directly to AI services (Qwen and DeepSeek) with API keys that you enter yourself, so you need your own keys and an agreement with those providers.
t.whoText: The app is built around people who find a touch screen hard to use:
who: blind and low-vision users, who can control it without looking at the screen
people with limited use of their hands, who can use a remote control, a keyboard or one large on-screen button
anyone who wants hands-free voice control
how: A Bluetooth remote control (fob) or the keys of a keyboard, also with the screen off
A large button on the screen and the Android accessibility button
Your voice: hold or tap to record, then release to send
t.howText: The app uses the Android accessibility service only to receive the presses of the remote control and keyboard that you set up. It does not read the screen or other apps.
t.downloadIntro: Requires Android %ANDROID% or newer. The app is not in Google Play. You install an APK file that you download from GitHub Releases.
t.noAlpha: No alpha build has been published yet.
t.noStable: There is no stable build yet. Everything is alpha.
t.buildsNone: No builds have been published yet.
t.buildsNote: Only the three newest alpha builds and the builds marked stable are kept. Older builds are removed.
install: Download the APK file on your phone (use the download button above).
Open it. Android asks to allow installing apps from this source (your browser or file manager). Allow it for this install.
Android Play Protect may warn that the app is unknown. This is expected for an app outside Google Play.
Open Audio Agent. When it asks for the microphone and for notifications, allow them.
Enter your own keys: Settings, Keys. The button "How to get keys" in the app explains it. Then press "Check".
Optional: compare the SHA-256 value in the table with the file you downloaded.
t.installText: These are the short steps. The full guide explains every screen in plain words: how to get and enter your keys, how to turn on the remote control, and what to do when something does not work.
t.guideDescription: A step-by-step user guide for Audio Agent: what you need, install, keys, first conversation, remote control, commands, long conversations and documents, and troubleshooting.
use: Hold the big Record button on the Agent tab, speak, and let go. The answer is spoken aloud.
Short commands work at once: "pause", "next track", "set a timer for five minutes", "what time is it".
Ask for music, reminders, notes and lists, calendar events, weather, calling a contact or a route.
Use a remote control, a keyboard key, the notification button or a long press of the power button, so you do not have to touch the screen.
Say "what can you do" to hear spoken help.
t.useGuideText: The user guide explains all of this step by step, for beginners, including blind and low-vision users.
t.privacyText: There is no developer server, no account, no analytics and no advertising. Your voice and requests go from your phone straight to the AI providers whose keys you entered. This site makes no requests to third parties.
t.contactText: Report problems on the issues page of the project, or write to the contact address.
t.footer: Audio Agent is an alpha-stage project. No tracking on this site.
t.licenseNote: The site text and the privacy policy are CC BY 4.0. The app builds are all rights reserved, free for personal use. The source code is not published.

v2.heroLead: Press, speak, and your Android phone answers aloud. Made first for blind and low-vision people, and for anyone who can't easily use their hands.
v2.heroMeta: Free for personal use · alpha · made by one person · no account
v2.heroToday: Everything on this page works today, except what is marked Alpha.
v2.exCap: One press, then just keep talking
v2.ex2: Two things: the dentist at ten, and a call with Marta at four.
v2.ex3: Add milk to the shopping list.
v2.s1Lead: It's one chat, not single commands. Every new question carries on from the last answer.
v2.s1Loop: Step 4 goes back to step 2: same chat, it keeps what was said
s1Text: Press the button, in any way you can press it.
Ask again. You are back at step 2, in the same chat, and it keeps what was said.
v2.s1Det: You can stop, replay or skip an answer, or ask it to rephrase. Light and dark themes, four text sizes and a black screen for driving.
v2.s2H: One button can do six things.
v2.s2Lead: Press it any way you can. Each kind of press can do something different, and you choose what.
s2Text: Ways to press: the screen, a Bluetooth remote or switch, a keyboard key, a long press of the power button, a notification button.
They all lead to one button.
One button, six kinds of press: tap; hold; double tap; double tap and hold; triple tap; triple tap and hold. Each can do a different action.
v2.s2Det: If a remote has more buttons, you can give each one its own function, for example stop, replay, skip the answer, rephrase or new chat. You set this up on the screen, button by button, and the app can learn which button you pressed.
v2.s3Lead: Long chats keep going: a running summary keeps the start in mind. Along the way you can do more with it.
s3Items: Attach a document and ask about it
Find an old chat by its topic
Start a new chat, or go back
v2.s3Mem: Memory: it remembers what you told it
s3Text: Attach a text or Markdown document and ask about it by voice.
Find an old chat by its topic.
Start a new chat, or go back to the previous one.
v2.s3TextHead: Your chat, one long line. Along it you can:
v2.s3TextMem: Memory: it remembers what you told it about yourself.
v2.s3Det: Add a document from the clipboard or with Share. Hear the topics of your recent chats. Memory: you can see, edit and delete everything it remembers, or switch it off.
v2.s4H: Everyday things, in the same chat.
v2.s4Lead: You don't switch apps or modes. Just say it.
v2.t2p: “Remind me to buy bread when I'm near the shop.”
v2.t5p: “Call Anna.” The dialer opens; you press call.
s4Text: Music on your phone: “Play my evening playlist.”
Timers and reminders, by time or place: “Remind me to buy bread when I'm near the shop.”
Notes and lists: “Add eggs to the shopping list.”
Weather, news, web search: “What's the weather tomorrow?”
Calendar and calls: “Call Anna.” The dialer opens; you press call.
Routes and saved places: “Take me home.”
v2.s4Det: Music: artist, album, track, playlists, pause, next, volume. Calendar: read your events and add one. A reminder by place needs location permission. Search and news need a DeepSeek key.
v2.smsText: Reads your unread text messages aloud, with numbers and codes hidden.
v2.s5Lead: You bring your own keys. Your voice and text go straight from your phone to the AI services, and nowhere else.
v2.s5Arrow: voice and text, with your keys
v2.s5Line: No account · No analytics · No ads
s5Text: Your phone holds your chats, your API keys and what it remembers.
Voice and text go from your phone, with your keys, straight to the AI services: Qwen for voice recognition and speech, DeepSeek for web search and news.
No account, no analytics, no ads.
v2.dlLead: Free for personal use, for Android. It is an alpha made by one person: some things will break, and your feedback shapes it.
v2.dlNeed: You need: an Android phone with Android %ANDROID% or newer, and your own API keys. Voice recognition and speech use Qwen; web search and news use DeepSeek. You enter the keys yourself, and the setup guide shows how to get them.
v2.dlStore: The app is not in Google Play. You install an APK file that you download from GitHub Releases.
v2.moreLead: The pages above are the overview. Here is the rest, and the full guide explains every screen step by step.
